sentences.text: Constitution Of India Seeking The ... vs Sujatha on 17 July, 2023

The Hon'Ble Smt Justice V. Sujatha
 Writ Petition No.16437 of 2023
Order:
This writ petition came to be filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India seeking the
following relief:
"....to issue Writ order or direction more particularly in the nature of Mandamus
decla

ring the action of the Respondents in collecting life tax @ 18 percent coming to Rs.20,88,010/- (Rupees twenty lakh eighty eight thousand and ten only) on the GST of Rs.21,94,594/- (Rupees twenty one lakh ninety four thousand five hundred and ninety four) and Compensation Cess of 15,67,568/- (Rupees fifteen lakh sixty seven thousand five hundred and sixty eight only) along with the cost of Mercedes-Benz GLS 400 D 4MATIC Registration No.AP 39 RR 6899 with Chassis No.W1N1679236M013118, Engine No.65692980246175, instead of the "cost of motor vehicle" of INR 7,837,837/ alone, contrary to Section 3(2) (Second proviso) of the Andhra Pradesh Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1963 R/w Sixth Schedule (hereinafter called the "Act") and the Andhra Pradesh Motor Vehicles Taxation Rules 1963,
(hereinafter called the "Rules") as illegal, arbitrary, without jurisdiction and violative of Articles 14, 19, 265 and 300A of the Constitution of India and consequently direct Respondents to refund INR 6,77,189/- (Rupees six lakh seventy seven thousand one hundred and eighty nine only) being the excess tax paid by the Petitioners along with an interest rate of 24 percent per annum from the date of Temporary Registration for such reliefs and pass....."
2. During hearing, learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Government Pleader for Transport and the learned Government Pleader for Finance & Planning submitted that the issue involved in this petition is squarely covered by the common order of this Court in Writ Petition Nos.12089 of 2019 and 3049 of 2021, dated 13.06.2023.

sentences.text: However, learned Government Pleader for Transport has submitted that they are intending to file Writ Appeal.

3. In view of the above said submissions of all the learned counsel, this petition is allowed in terms of the said common order dated 13.06.2023 passed in W.P.Nos.12089 of 2019 and 3049 of 2021, by directing the respondents to refund a sum of Rs.6,77,189/- to the petitioner, which were collected in excess of the life tax payable by the petitioner under the Sixth Schedule to the Act on the invoice sale price, within a period of four (4) weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
Miscellaneous petitions, pending, if any, in this Writ Petition shall stand closed.
The Registry is directed to attach a copy of the common order in W.P.Nos.12089 of 2019 and 3049 of 2021 dated 13.06.2023, to this order.
